newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Deutsche's DMG confirms it in Svyazinvest group.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche's DMG confirms it in Svyazinvest group.

text.p: Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, the investment banking division of Germany's biggest bank Deutsche Bank AG, is part of the Mustcom consortium which won a 25 percent plus one share stake in Russian telecoms holding company Svyazinvest, a senior DMG official said on Friday.

Asked whether DMG was part of Mustcom, DMG's Moscow chief executive Nick Jordan replied: "Yes." He declined to say who else was in the consortium. "I will leave that to Mr Potanin to describe. He is the head of the consortium," he said in a reference to Vladimir Potanin, the president of Uneximbank.

Vladimir Malin, deputy chairman of the Russian Federal Property Fund, said previously Mustcom had won the stake, Russia's biggest privatisation, with a $1.875 billion bid against a starting price of $1.18 billion. There was one other bid.

Malin said Moscow investment bank Renaissance Capital was one of the owners of Mustcom, but gave no other details. Earlier a spokesman for Uneximbank, Russia's third biggest bank, said it had won the tender in a consortium with its investment bank Bank MFK (ICFI) and Interros Group affiliates, Renaissance Capital and Deutsche.
